settings.definition_quote: We consider a time-slotted system with one player and $N$ independent arms. At each time slot, the player selects (activates) $K(<N)$ arms and gets a certain amount of rewards according to the current state of the arm. Each arm is modeled as a discrete-time, irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain with finite state space.

source.label: theoremRA:K=1
source.quote: Assume all arms are modeled as finite state, irreducible, aperiodic and reversible Markov chains. All the states (rewards) are positive. The expected regret with Algorithm 1 after $n$ time slots is at most $Z_1 G(n)\ln{n} + Z_2 \ln{n} + Z_3 G(n) + Z_4$, where $Z_1,Z_2,Z_3,Z_4$ are constants only related to $P_i, i=1,2,\cdots, N$

results.notes: Weak regret t*mu_star - E[R(t)] against best stationary arm; mapped to pseudo_regret. Near-logarithmic since G(n) grows arbitrarily slowly.

symbols.Z_1p: Z_1' instance constant (Z_1 with B_q replaced by B_1)

conditions: arms are finite-state, irreducible, aperiodic and reversible Markov chains

source.quote: The system model is the same as that in Theorem \ref{theoremRA:K=1}. In Algorithm 1, if $B_i \equiv \lceil \max \{\frac{2C_P}{\mu^{\sigma(1)}-\mu^{\sigma{(2)}}}, \frac{C_P}{\mu^{\sigma(l)}},l=1,2,\cdots,N\}\rceil$ then the expected regret after n time slots is at most $Z_1' B_1\ln{n} + Z_2' \ln{n} + Z_3' B_1 + Z_4'$

results.notes: Logarithmic regret; the learner must know bounds on C_P (stationary distribution/rewards) and the gap to set B_i (not expressible in learner_knows vocabulary).

source.label: theoremRA:K
source.quote: Assume all arms are modeled as finite state, irreducible, aperiodic and reversible Markov chains. All the states (rewards) are positive. The expected regret with Algorithm \ref{alg:sensing2} after $n$ time steps is at most $Z_5 G(n)\ln{n} + Z_6 \ln{n} + Z_7 G(n) + Z_8$

results.notes: Paper's N arms = canonical K, paper's K plays = canonical m. Weak regret mapped to pseudo_regret.

conditions: arms are finite-state, irreducible, aperiodic and reversible Markov chains

source.quote: The system model is the same as that in Theorem \ref{theoremRA:K}. In Algorithm \ref{alg:sensing2}, if $B_i \equiv \lceil \max\{\frac{2C_P}{\mu^{\sigma(K)}-\mu^{\sigma{(K+1)}}},\frac{C_P}{\mu^{\sigma(l)}},l=1,2,\cdots,N\}\rceil$ then the expected regret after n time slots is at most $Z_5' B_1\ln{n} + Z_6' \ln{n} + Z_7' B_1 + Z_8'$

results.notes: Logarithmic regret when bounds on C_P and the K-th gap are known to set B_i.
